newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka index, turnover up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka index, turnover up on foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on healthy turnover, supported by foreign buying of a blue chip finance stock, brokers said. The all share index closed 1.56 points up at 622.48. Though losses led gains by 20 to 17, an 11-rupee rise in highly capitalised blue chip Development Finance, kept the index up.
Development Finance closed at 280 rupees on 150,700 shares.
"The broker had to pay up to get a big volume of Development Finance shares," said a broker who declined to be named.

Turnover was 68.99 million rupees on 3.1 million shares, supported by the parcel of Development Finance and two million shares of Forbes Ceylon. Foreign buying was worth 56.99 million rupees, and selling 10.8 million rupees.
Investors were still not sure if the correction which began on January 27, after the all share passed 630 points, was over.

"Though we believe the index could fall a bit more, we are buying slowly among very liquid manufacturing and finance stocks, where there are some good values anyway," said Derendra Abayaratna, fund manager of Century Growth Fund.
